writing-for-agents.note: SOURCE-EDITS.md is astack-authored and locates the owning repository before handing off to its local workflow. Astack authoring and delivery are repository-local so installed writing guidance remains usable in other repositories. A user-invoked description may keep one trigger clause because astack-help routes on installed frontmatter. Harness notes drop OpenCode because astack does not install it. That also drops the rule to write every description for the model, which only OpenCode required.

unslop.note: Rules verbatim as of c1c0a32; rule numbers are stable ids other skills cite. Step 1 adds a done condition. Keeps the text that upstream 00b14f1 and 70b2dc8 cut.

principles.note: The 23 principle skills present at c1c0a32 as plain files under one model-invoked index. This entry does not cover Explain the Number, which upstream added later. Frontmatter removed, applicability retained in the bodies, links adapted to local files, and unavailable skill references removed. Headings use sentence case and duplicate applicability statements are removed. Adaptations put migration preconditions before the rule, bound root-cause fixes to the task's scope, preserve external-constraint explanations, clarify boundary guarantees, and consolidate the mechanism hierarchy. Autonomy follows the user's authorization and approval preferences; context guidance follows writing-for-agents. Other edits group failing-test and fix commits into one verified unit, allow reuse of a concrete tool, and narrow attack-the-premise to actor imbalances without treating an even census as proof. Earlier astack-added completion tests and one-off reply notes are removed. Upstream examples for pure functions, idempotency, and the reader-load/context-window cross-reference are retained. Minimize Reader Load links to Deep Modules, whose Matt Pocock provenance is recorded under codebase-design. Replaces the upstream cuts in 00b14f1, 08bd59b, 99743e9, b0b9c7a, and 70b2dc8 with astack's own trim, which keeps every rule. Several upstream cuts, in 08bd59b and 99743e9, leave a rule only in the frontmatter description astack removed. Against e5136d8, keeps the five assertion shapes as an inspection list, the idempotency pattern list with a lock bullet safe from PID reuse, the attack-the-premise actor narrowing, and the fix-root-causes scope bound.

open-pr.note: Adapted under the global Pull Requests policy. Keeps narrow PRs, stack relationships, coherent commits, no-comments, technical-writing, unslop, title guidance, and default description sections. Cursor forge and deslop removed; Gitleaks hook install and T3 Code PR linking added. Links shared astack guidance for reusing, scoping, and publishing PR test results, including delegated runs and the tested commit. Runs review-pr after the PR exists, so its review record posts on GitHub.

review-pr.note: Preserves the independent Standards and Spec axes and Fowler smell baseline. Parent-owned repairs address implementation handoffs that previously stopped after reporting findings. An outside-provider Correctness axis gives delegated implementations cross-model bug review without full hardening. Posting the review record is its own step because agents often skipped a closing pointer to posting.md. The pass limit exists because a fix-and-review run that keeps finding problems may need a different direction. The Standards axis also compares screenshots of a visual change with the shipped page, because reviewers that read only code passed off-brand pages.

technical-writing.note: Verbatim as of c1c0a32 apart from dropping disable-model-invocation, a shorter model-facing description, unslop pointers as sibling links, a rule 26 citation without the line against editing unslop, "swarm logs" shortened to "logs", the tab-indentation rule removed, and astack's own trim, which replaces the upstream cuts in 00b14f1, 23e4138, and 70b2dc8 and keeps every rule.

no-comments.note: The Comment Sicko subagent is gone; its keep list and flag rules are the skill body, applied by the agent itself. The /how, /why, and /architect calls became read-the-history and sketch-the-shape instructions; principle references point at ../principles files. Keeps a suppression that the repository's agent rule table approves for that file and rule, with an approver and an unexpired date, so no-comments does not undo an exception that correct recorded. Applies only the keep list to comments written during other work, because its description and the global instructions send agents here whenever they add or change a comment.

harden-pr.license: MIT, kept in skills/harden-pr/LICENSE-pstack, LICENSE-mattpocock, and LICENSE-gstack
harden-pr.note: Uses generated gstack review Markdown without its generator or global runtime. Scope follows current user requirements. Findings require evidence rather than numerical scores. PR transport retains earlier pstack and Matt material. Keeps the merge-authorization rules that upstream 08bd59b cut. The Matt element pins 153fc1b (daa01d8^), the last commit with resolving-merge-conflicts; its substance lives in pr-work.md.

grilling.note: Preserves the design-tree interview, frontier rounds, recommendations, and shared-understanding checkpoint. Removes decorative emoji from the question template. The description triggers only when the user asks, as writing-for-agents requires of a skill whose procedure is an interview. Allows direct factual lookups and delegates independent exploration that can run alongside the interview.

improve-codebase-architecture.note: Preserves exploration, visual candidate reports, user selection, grilling, domain-model updates, and optional interface alternatives. Uses local skill links, tolerates absent project documentation, and adds targeted astack principle references. Reports use t3-preview, inline assets, dark styling, and plain candidate sections. Reads the Deep Modules principle and permits boundary terminology. DEEPENING.md and DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md are tracked under codebase-design, their upstream source. Consolidates report instructions in HTML-REPORT.md and glossary/ADR actions in domain-modeling. Reads principles at the relevant decisions and applies the deletion test from Deep Modules instead of restating it. Passes identified glossary and ADR locations to domain-modeling. The report links to DEEPENING.md for dependency classification.

domain-modeling.note: Preserves glossary updates, multiple contexts, and selective ADR creation with both format references. Uses sentence-case headings and reference-style links in the sample glossary map so example repository paths are not treated as installed skill dependencies. Consolidates glossary locations and format in GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md and ADR locations, numbering, and examples in ADR-FORMAT.md. Keeps ADR eligibility and lazy document creation in SKILL.md; removes repeated criteria and directory trees. Triggers on defining or challenging domain terms rather than discussing them, so a question about terms stays read-only. Uses glossary and ADR locations identified by the caller or project instructions, retaining upstream defaults otherwise. Reads and updates an existing CONTEXT.md or CONTEXT-MAP.md in place, because repositories set up before upstream d80fa0f keep the earlier names.

codebase-design.license: MIT, copied from repository-root LICENSE to skills/principles/LICENSE-mattpocock and skills/improve-codebase-architecture/LICENSE-mattpocock
codebase-design.note: The shared reference is now the Deep Modules principle; its workflows live under improve-codebase-architecture. Removes skill frontmatter and the separate Codex display metadata, adds an applicability trigger, and uses sentence-case headings. Consolidates Relationships into the glossary and repeated seam definitions into the principle. Removes the blanket restriction on boundary terminology. Pure-function and assertion guidance point to Boundary Discipline and Test Behavior, Not Implementation. Interface exploration reads Exhaust the Design Space and passes applicable caller principles to designers. Old tests are removed only after their behavior is covered at the new interface. Designer briefs include project domain vocabulary when available. Replaces the claim that fewer methods require fewer tests with guidance on simplifying test setup.

worktree-cleanup.note: Adapted for model invocation on cleanup, resource audits, and lane closeout. Checks unfinished work first and reports blockers before cleanup or handoff writes. Uses Git inventory, T3 thread ownership, and task resource evidence instead of Cursor-specific auditing. Covers processes, Docker storage, disposable test databases, and t3-preview HTML and quick tunnels. Preserves shared resources and the daily-driver T3 connection. Adds preview ownership records; simulator and cache cleanup remains optional. Prose trimmed to task-specific rules and teardown hazards.

ship-pr.note: Adapted as ship-pr, a model-invoked entry point for landing an existing PR or stack. Reuses the shared PR follow-through procedure and existing review evidence. Removes the mandatory independent verification pass and separate verdict protocol; refreshes verification when evidence is missing or changes invalidate it. Retains safeguards against merging unverified head changes.

how.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/how/LICENSE
how.note: Preserves the upstream opening directive, simple and complex delegation paths, separate explorer and explainer prompts, and explanation structure. Shortens the description to the 200-character cap. Replaces Cursor Task parameters and fixed models with available subagent tools and a read-only direct fallback. Uses portable file-search instructions, validated reference links, and sentence-case headings. Makes explorer findings conditional in the explainer prompt so the direct-explain path works. Replaces the upstream cuts in 00b14f1 and 08bd59b with astack's own trim, which keeps every rule.

why.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/why/LICENSE
why.note: Preserves the upstream investigation workflow, default parallel source sweep, confidence framework, separate investigator and synthesizer prompts, and all source playbooks. Shortens the description, adapts tool discovery and delegation to the active harness, permits explicitly scoped investigations, and reports unavailable sources as gaps. Treats provider tools and warehouse schemas as examples to verify. Uses validated links and sentence-case headings. Replaces the upstream cuts in 00b14f1 and 08bd59b with astack's own trim, which keeps every rule.

teach.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/teach/LICENSE
teach.note: Preserves the upstream teaching directive, five-step conversational workflow, progressive diagrams, and concrete examples. Shortens the description, reads how and why by sibling paths, scopes investigation before dispatch, and returns findings for a single teaching explanation. Adapts image generation to available tools and the user's requested colors. Links the existing unslop skill.

reflect.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/reflect/LICENSE
reflect.note: Preserves the upstream three review lenses, separate reviewer and synthesizer prompts, durable-learning criteria, and selected-edit workflow. Adapts transcript discovery and delegation to the active harness with direct fallbacks. Removes the finding quota, limits missed-trigger tuning to model-invoked skills, and files backlog issues only when requested. Routes authoring through writing-for-agents, shared lessons to principles, and approved astack improvements through the source-editing PR workflow. Honors prior edit authorization. Updates the synthesizer's trigger examples for astack metadata. Retains the text upstream 00b14f1 cut, because astack trims its own copies separately without dropping rules.

correct.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/correct/LICENSE-pstack
correct.note: Upstream assumes the agent owns the repository. astack's scope and destructive-action rules do not, so a diagnosis-only request changes nothing, old ways that external users depend on stay, and only the operator grants an exception. Exceptions live in the rule table because no-comments deletes justification comments on the line.

retro.license: MIT, copied from repository-root LICENSE to skills/reflect/LICENSE-mattpocock
retro.note: Imports only the automated-checks, no-ops, and information-access categories, as a tooling-lens addition in reflect. Reflect is transcript-scoped, so each finding needs session evidence, and a no-op must be an instruction the agent followed so a broken rule is not deleted.

create-verification-skill.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/create-verification-skill/LICENSE
create-verification-skill.note: Preserves the upstream creation workflow, complete feature-map examples, and maintenance procedure under one entry point. Shortens the description to a trigger on requests to create or maintain a verification skill, because a start on the agent's own judgment would generate a skill and drive the app unasked. Replaces Cursor-only paths with project skill conventions. Adds shared authoring guidance and conditional verification, automation, idempotency, and testing principle links. Adapts delegation with a direct fallback, respects startup scope and isolation, reports unreachable features as unverified, and opens maintenance PRs when requested. Splits the maintenance live-pass paragraph so its health, evidence, and cleanup requirements are readable.

architect.note: Arena owns candidate comparison. Architect retains design criteria and returns to the caller before implementation. UI exploration follows astack static-mock selection.

implement.license: MIT, kept in skills/implement/LICENSE-pstack and skills/implement/LICENSE-mattpocock
implement.note: The pstack Feature playbook supplies task ownership and delegation. Matt supplies TDD and implementation checks. Multi-phase work reuses the existing execution store so switching owners or workflows does not create competing state. Replaces the upstream cuts in 70b2dc8 and b0b9c7a with astack's own trim, which keeps every rule.

tdd.license: MIT, kept in skills/tdd/LICENSE-pstack and skills/tdd/LICENSE-mattpocock
tdd.note: Matt supplies the main skill and test-quality references. Pstack supplies BUG-FIX.md. Existing agreed test boundaries carry forward. Refactoring after green is allowed when it simplifies code without changing behavior. Replaces the upstream cuts in b0b9c7a and 70b2dc8 with astack's own trim, which keeps every rule.

to-spec.note: Delivers where the user asks, to the project's local location for implementation specs, or in the conversation, instead of Matt-specific setup and tracker labels. Story coverage scales to the feature instead of a quota that could invent requirements. Drops upstream's disable-model-invocation and Codex policy, because publishing to an issue tracker or another external system needs the user's request. In projects whose test files are specs, a spec request that does not ask for an implementation spec gets a test, because Codex reads the skill whenever a request mentions a spec.

prototype.license: MIT, kept in skills/prototype/LICENSE-pstack and skills/prototype/LICENSE-mattpocock
prototype.note: Matt supplies logic and UI exploration. Pstack supplies scratch isolation. Variants run in a scratch copy of the real app, and the user views a static screenshot gallery so no server has to stay up.

diagnosing-bugs.note: Captured-artifact analysis bypasses the runnable-reproduction gate, but does not verify a fix. Early code reading can help build a loop. Theories remain provisional. Diagnosis-only completion requires findings and probe cleanup, not a code fix. Pstack references are recorded under debugging-forensics.

implementation-slicing.note: Only vertical-slice and blocking-dependency guidance is retained in the existing Sequence Verifiable Units principle. No standalone to-tickets skill, tracker workflow, or ticket templates are installed. The rest of the principle retains its pstack provenance under principles.

wizard.note: Retains the upstream process, Bash template, example stage, and Codex metadata. Shortens the description to the 200-character cap, reuses agreed scope instead of requiring repeated confirmation, and limits CI and local writes to their agreed destinations. Adds secret redaction guidance and documents the literal single-line dotenv subset. write_env keeps writing that subset instead of upstream's single-quoted form, whose `'\''` escape is shell syntax rather than dotenv, and does not set $KEY. It resolves a symlinked .env and replaces the target by rename in its directory, keeping the target's mode, instead of upstream's truncate-and-copy, which leaves the file empty or partial if the copy is interrupted. A signal trap removes the temporary file, which holds every value and may escape a .env ignore rule. ask uses Readline only when input is a terminal, because upstream prompts through `read -p`, which prints nothing when input is not a terminal. It turns completion off through a temporary inputrc, because bash 3.2 ignores bind in scripts and Tab would otherwise splice file names into a value. The template preserves input whitespace, stops on EOF, quotes supported dotenv values, decodes existing quotes without evaluation, and rejects unsupported syntax before writes. Removes narration and decorative comments while retaining public helper contracts and the stage marker. Offline tests cover reruns, captured secret payloads, EOF, unsupported values, and action-only stages.

orchestrate.note: Retains the original Bun runtime and lockfile as an exception to astack's Python convention. Keeps Graphite, which upstream ce649c0 removed, and adds a GitHub adapter beside it. Shared ownership, retained drain batches, and verifier precedence support recovery across sessions without losing evidence. The CLI records claims. The coordinator still judges them.

multi-phase-plan.note: The checker uses the Python standard library for astack portability. Risk-sized scenarios replace fixed lane and model quotas. Performance exemptions need reasons. Stable probe IDs connect plan checks to executable commands without making the checker judge their adequacy. The checker also carries pstack 87c8103 and 86c2448 ahead of this pin.

wayfinder.note: TRACKER.md retains only wayfinding operations from Matt's local tracker. A coordinator serializes local claims because Markdown lacks atomic tracker operations. Cancellation does not satisfy dependents, and invalidated decisions retain their history.

show-me-your-work.note: Corrective rows resolve the upstream conflict between append-only history and deleting errors. Incompatible headers are rejected to preserve older four-column logs. The execution owner serializes writes because the helper has no lock. Keeps rejecting an existing empty log, which upstream 70b2dc8 treats as new.

handoff.license: MIT, kept in skills/handoff/LICENSE-mattpocock and skills/handoff/LICENSE-pstack
handoff.note: Standalone tasks retain Matt's temporary note. Planned execution and decision maps reuse their existing records to avoid competing state. Pickup reuses evidence only when it still applies, resolving upstream tension between avoiding repeated checks and proving inherited claims.

investigation.note: Extends the original how/why routing to diagnosis and captured artifacts because technical questions may arrive as failure reports or profiles. The inquiry remains read-only.

bug-fix.note: Reuses diagnosing-bugs and tdd rather than defining a second diagnosis loop. Failing-before evidence is required without mandating a separate failing commit. Delivery stays within the task authorization. Keeps the text that upstream b0b9c7a cut.

perf-issue.note: Repeated comparable measurements distinguish improvements from noise. Correctness checks accompany performance measurements. Keeps the eight strategy families that upstream e43c7ee replaced with bare performance mantras, because each family names the signal that earns it an attempt. The families take the mantras' cheapest-first order and stop rule, with Divide and conquer and Redundancy both under "Do it concurrently".

debugging-forensics.note: Native queries can replace mandatory SQLite conversion. Retention alone does not establish a leak. Paired captures alone do not prove causality. Runtime instrumentation is a write and needs the corresponding scope, despite the upstream read-only label.

arena.note: Provider CLI tasks return read-only proposals that the parent materializes in isolated worktrees. Same-provider and direct fallbacks disclose missing diversity or independence. Keeps the same-provider judge fallback that upstream ab1f702 removed, and the text that upstream 00b14f1 cut; astack trims its own copies without dropping rules.

hillclimb.note: Minimum attempts apply when requested. Repeated confirmation guards early wins otherwise. Existing logs and handoffs preserve progress without promising automatic wake. Remeasuring a moved base keeps base changes from counting as the run's gains. The accept step applies the checklist's questions 4 and 7 to the harness counts, which upstream states only in the checklist, and skips them when the harness prints no counts, as under hillclimb-council's vote. A harness for a metric other than performance is vetted with Explain the Number, because the benchmark checklist assumes a timing benchmark.

benchmark-checklist.note: A perf-issue reference rather than its own user-invoked skill, which drops upstream's direct /benchmark-checklist entry point. Other measurement reaches it through Explain the Number. Drops the section on how perf-issue and hillclimb use it, which both skills state. The busy-machine line and question 4's read-only exception follow astack's scope rules: stopping another owner's process is destructive, and read-only work excludes instrumentation.

refactoring.note: Keeps the text that upstream b0b9c7a cut.

brag-slim.note: Full /brag is not imported because it depends on Hyperframes and its bundled music has unverified redistribution terms. On Opus 5.5, /brag already runs brag-slim unless the user asks for `--full` or `--voice`. The description drops the /brag hand-off because astack does not install /brag. Step 2 waits for plan approval because a render takes minutes and the storyboard is the cheapest point to change direction. The output directory ignores itself because a run inside a repository otherwise leaves about 0.5 GB of untracked frames that `git add -A` would commit. astack makes the ad shape the only shape because it uses brag-slim to sell products to customers. The checker reads lines in order because checking each line alone at 0.3s per word passes multi-line beats that viewers find too fast.

full-send.note: astack-authored skill. Omits tstack's proof and scope rules because prove-it-works, implement, bug-fix, and laziness-protocol cover them. Allows --admin, which tstack bans, at the user's choice.

council.note: User-invoked, like most astack skills. Default members are Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol at xhigh, at the user's choice, because the user's providers are Claude and Codex. Outside T3 Code, dispatch follows arena's provider execution because a harness's own subagents cannot reach another provider. The Members and Review headings let hillclimb-council link to them. Upstream's review loop never ends when a delegate keeps requesting out-of-scope work, so declined requests can end it.
